title: Herald Web Story: "Lab Leak Reported in Lindgren"

fields.label: developing
fields.headline: Lab leak reported in Lindgren; vials missing from freezer
fields.dek: A graduate student was sent to the clinic, and students say the university has not told people in the building whether they are at risk.
fields.heroImageBrief: exterior of a modern brick and glass university science building on a clear autumn day, students walking past, editorial campus newspaper photo
fields.heroCaption: The Lindgren Life Sciences Building on the Halvorsen State University campus.
fields.body:
MARLOW FALLS, Iowa — A biological leak in a third-floor laboratory of the Lindgren Life Sciences Building sent a graduate student to the clinic this morning, and vials were reported missing from a freezer one floor up, according to two students who work in the building. The university did not respond to requests for comment by publication time.

Students on the third floor said a door near the shared lab space was taped off mid-morning with a biohazard sign and a paper reading "STOP WORK." One student, who asked not to be named because they work in the building, said a graduate student was "walked to the clinic" shortly after 9 a.m.

A second student said a laboratory on the fourth floor had found that "a bunch of vials" were missing from a freezer during a count this morning. It was not clear what the vials held or whether the two events are connected.

A post on the HSU Campus Forum that has drawn more than 400 upvotes described the incident as a "LAB LEAK IN LINDGREN" and told readers: "If you were in Lindgren today, go get tested. They won't send an HSUAlert because they're covering it up." A reply to a separate social media post asked whether the leak involved "select agents," a federal category of regulated organisms. The Herald has not confirmed that the university works with select agents.

The Herald emailed University Communications at 10:08 a.m. and again at 11:05 a.m. asking whether anyone was hurt and whether people in the building were at risk. As of publication, the office had not replied. The head of the Department of Biology declined to comment when reached by phone and referred questions to University Communications.

No HSUAlert had been sent to campus as of 12:45 p.m. Students in the building said they had received no written update about the leak or about whether they should leave the floor.

Several students said they were worried about colleagues. "Nobody's telling us anything," one wrote on social media. "Are we supposed to be in here?"

The Herald will update this story if the university responds. Readers with information can contact the newsroom at news@halvorsenherald.example.

instructorNote: Misinformation inject: the story says vials are missing, although they were found in ULT-L4-12 at 11:50, and calls the event a "leak" four times with no evidence of a release outside the room. Watch for three things: (1) the PIO sends the cleared holding statement with IO approval, with no worker, lab or organism named and no "no risk" promise; (2) the PIO asks the Herald for a correction that names the errors without repeating "leak" as its headline; and (3) the PIO posts one forum reply after the BSO confirms the facts and logs every statement for the 14-day account. Also read aloud a text from the president's office to the IO at 12:55: a regent on the research committee has seen the Herald story and wants a call today. Watch that the IO phones the committee chair with the cleared facts only.
